content.value_statement: Cloud teams often overspend because usage, ownership, and pricing choices are hard to track. This skill guides rightsizing, tagging, budget alerts, and pricing model decisions.
actual_capabilities: Explains cost optimization strategies for AWS, Azure, and GCP.
Provides rightsizing, idle resource cleanup, and autoscaling guidance.
Recommends tagging, budget alerts, anomaly detection, and cost dashboards.
Compares reserved capacity, savings plans, spot instances, and committed use discounts.
Includes Terraform-style examples for lifecycle policies, tags, budgets, and autoscaling.
limitations: Does not connect to cloud accounts or retrieve live billing data.
Does not validate provider prices against current regional rate sheets.
Does not generate a complete FinOps operating model by itself.
Example infrastructure snippets require review before production use.

use_cases.title: Reduce Monthly Cloud Waste
use_cases.description: Identify idle resources, oversized instances, and storage lifecycle opportunities before the next billing cycle.

use_cases.title: Create Cost Governance Standards
use_cases.description: Define tagging, budget alerts, anomaly monitoring, and review routines for accountable cloud spending.

use_cases.title: Compare Pricing Commitments
use_cases.description: Evaluate reserved instances, savings plans, spot capacity, and committed use discounts for steady workloads.

prompt_templates.title: Find Quick Savings
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the cost-optimization skill to review my current monthly cloud spend of [amount]. Ask for missing details, then list quick savings actions by provider.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Tagging Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the cost-optimization skill to design a tagging plan for [cloud provider]. Include ownership, environment, project, cost center, and review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Commitment Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the cost-optimization skill to compare savings plans, reserved instances, spot capacity, and on-demand pricing for [workload profile].

prompt_templates.title: Design Governance Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the cost-optimization skill to create a multi-cloud cost governance workflow for [organization]. Include dashboards, alerts, rightsizing, approvals, and review cadence.

output_examples.input: Review our AWS bill for short-term savings opportunities.
output: A prioritized savings list covering idle resources, storage lifecycle changes, and rightsizing checks.
Recommended owner tags and budget alerts for monthly tracking.
Verification steps using Cost Explorer, Compute Optimizer, and weekly reviews.

output_examples.input: Create a cloud cost governance checklist for our platform team.
output: A checklist for tags, budgets, anomaly detection, reserved capacity reviews, and unused resource cleanup.
A suggested weekly and monthly review cadence.
Clear handoffs between platform, finance, and application teams.

output_examples.input: Compare cost strategies for a steady production workload.
output: A comparison of on-demand, reserved capacity, savings plans, and spot usage.
Guidance on commitment risk, workload stability, and fallback capacity.
A recommendation to validate utilization before purchasing commitments.

best_practices: Start with cost visibility, ownership tags, and budget alerts before changing infrastructure.
Validate utilization and reliability requirements before rightsizing or buying commitments.
Review savings opportunities on a fixed cadence with finance and engineering owners.
anti_patterns: Buying long-term commitments before confirming stable workload demand.
Deleting or downsizing resources without checking business criticality and recovery needs.
Using generic tags that do not map spend to accountable teams or services.

faq.question: Does this skill access my cloud billing account?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples, but it does not connect to AWS, Azure, or GCP.

faq.question: Can it calculate exact savings?
faq.answer: It can outline savings methods, but exact savings require current usage data and provider pricing.

faq.question: Which cloud providers are covered?
faq.answer: The skill covers AWS, Azure, and GCP, with some multi-cloud governance guidance.

faq.question: Is this useful for FinOps teams?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports tagging, budget alerts, anomaly detection, rightsizing, and commitment planning.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Are the infrastructure examples production ready?
faq.answer: No. Treat examples as starting points and review them against your cloud policies.
